subject: Request: temporary 4-day workweek / reduced hours — Maya Srinivasan
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary 4-day workweek / reduced hours — Maya Srinivasan

Hi Vivek and Monica,

I'm writing to request a formal, temporary accommodation as I transition back to full duties following my recent surgery. My physician has recommended a phased return for 6–8 weeks with fewer consecutive workdays to manage fatigue and recovery. Specifically I'm proposing a 4-day workweek (Mon–Thu) at 8 hours/day for the first 6 weeks, with the option to move to a 5-day reduced-hours schedule (6 hours/day) thereafter depending on how I am doing.

I've attached the signed doctor's note from Dr. Rao and a quick proposed schedule (proposed-schedule-4day.xlsx). I can be flexible with hours on the 4 working days (early shifts or compressed schedule) if it helps the team.

Key asks:
- Confirmation this temporary schedule can be approved under People Ops guidance
- Any forms HR needs me to complete (I filled out the initial intake but haven't submitted a formal light-duty form)
- Temporary coverage plan for the specific on-call rotations and weekly customer syncs (happy to work with Laura on coverage).

I want to ensure there's minimal disruption to the product launch the week of Oct 19 — I can handle async work and core planning but would appreciate protected recovery time in the afternoons.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary 4-day workweek / reduced hours — Maya Srinivasan

Maya — thanks for the note and the attachments. First, I'm glad the surgery went well and you're taking the right precautions during recovery.

Monica — can you confirm the standard People Ops process here? If there's a formal light-duty approval and a start date, let's get that scheduled. From a team perspective: Laura and I discussed and we can reassign the Wed customer sync to Laura for the first 6 weeks; Maya, please confirm which weekday you prefer off (Fri or Mon) for the 4-day option. Also, we'll identify a backup for the on-call rotation and rotate pager duties while you ramp up.

Maya — please let me and Laura know whether afternoons need to be protected daily (e.g., no meetings after 3pm) or if it's flexible. We'll document the temporary duties in the team doc so no customer-facing surprises.

I'll wait for Monica's guidance and the HR light-duty form. If approved, I suggest we kick the plan on Monday, Oct 12 to give a week for scheduling and calendar changes.

—Vivek
Director, Platform Engineering
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary 4-day workweek / reduced hours — Maya Srinivasan

Thanks for the heads up, Vivek and Maya.

We can accommodate a temporary 4-day workweek under Redwood's ADA-adjacent light-duty policy. Next steps:
1) Maya — please complete the light-duty form (attached as light-duty-form.pdf) and confirm the effective date and which day you prefer off (Mon or Fri).
2) We'll need the signed doctor's note (we have Dr. Rao's PDF attached) on file for the accommodation record.
3) HR will schedule a brief intake call (20 min) to document expectations and decline/approval terms. I propose Monday, Oct 5 at 10:30am PT or Tuesday, Oct 6 at 11am PT — which works for you?
4) We'll draft a temporary duties checklist and coverage plan; Laura, can you confirm coverage for customer syncs and who will be primary backup for the pager?

Operational guidance:
- Protected recovery window: Maya requested afternoons for rest — suggest "no internal meetings after 3pm" for first two weeks, then reassess.
- On-call: reduce Maya's escalation responsibility to advisory; primary pager rotation should exclude Maya for the first 4 weeks.

If everyone agrees, I'll create a formal accommodation record and route it for sign-off.

Regards,
Monica Patel
People Operations Manager
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary 4-day workweek / reduced hours — Maya Srinivasan

Maya — thanks for sharing the plan and apologies for the delay. I can take the Wed customer syncs and own the on-call primary for the first month; Arun will cover the weekly demo next Tuesday (I'm copying him on a separate thread).

Maya, I think taking Friday off would be better for sprint alignment (Mon work / Thu wrap / Fri rest), but I'm flexible if you prefer Monday off. I support "no meetings after 3pm" for the first two weeks and an internal checkpoint on Oct 26 to reassess. I'll update our team calendar and assign the backup tasks.

Laura
Principal PM, Platform
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary 4-day workweek / reduced hours — Maya Srinivasan

Thanks everyone — Friday off works best for my follow-up appointments, so let's go with Mon–Thu full days for the initial 6 weeks, with no internal meetings after 3pm. Monica, I can do the HR intake on Oct 6 at 11am PT.

I've uploaded the signed doctor's note to the HR drive and attached the proposed schedule. Vivek/Laura — I'll update my calendar with the adjusted availability and leave notes on the relevant Jira tickets so the team knows who to escalate to.

Appreciate the support.

—Maya
